ModifyBlockMultiplicative.issue: The sim replaces C#'s HISTORY QUERY with hand-rolled per-power state, and the two disagree about when the allowance resets. C# counts, on every call, History.Entries.OfType<BlockGainedEntry>() where e.HappenedThisTurn(base.CombatState) && e.Actor == target && e.Props.IsCardOrMonsterMove() && e.CardPlay != cardPlay (UnmovablePower.cs:35) -- so the window is the game's own turn window and the exclusion is 'gains from THIS card play do not count against it'. The sim keeps self._plays_used and self._active_card and resets them from on_player_turn_start (powers.py:1127-1130), which is player.py:169. Two divergences follow. (a) THE RESET SLOT: the sim's counter survives the whole enemy turn and is cleared only at the player's next turn start, while C#'s HappenedThisTurn window is the CombatState's, so any block the owner gains during the ENEMY turn from a card or move -- a turn-end auto-play under power/stampede, an on_enemy_turn effect -- lands in a different window on the two sides. (b) THE per-CardPlay EXCLUSION: C# compares CardPlay identities so a card played twice (Duplication, Throwing Axe) counts as TWO plays against the allowance, where the sim compares CARD identity (powers.py:1113) and its on_card_played bump fires once per card (combat.py:514, outside the play loop), so a doubled block card consumes ONE stack in the sim and two in the game -- hook_dispatch's G4 again, not re-verdicted, but here it means a doubled Iron Wave gets DOUBLE block twice in the sim and once in the game. Reachable: Unmovable is a ported Ironclad card (cards/unmovable.py:36) and Throwing Axe is a ported relic from the ported Tanx shrine.

guards.issue: RE-VERDICTED 2026-07-26 (relic-tier merge review): `faithful` -> `gap`, LIVE, grade B. The old rationale claimed unpowered block 'is not doubled on either side'. THAT IS FALSE ON THE C# SIDE. ValuePropExtensions.cs:23-26 defines IsCardOrMonsterMove as exactly `props.HasFlag(ValueProp.Move)` -- Move ALONE. It does not exclude Unpowered, so UnmovablePower.cs:27-30 deliberately PERMITS an Unpowered|Move block gain to reach the multiplier, the same looser gating src/Core/Models/Relics/Vambrace.cs:57 and src/Core/Models/Relics/PaelsLegion.cs:134 use (the game ships two PaelsLegion.cs; the relic is the Relics one). The sim's BlockCmd.apply gate (cmds.py:145) is is_powered_attack(props) -- Move AND NOT Unpowered -- so the sim never reaches the listener at all. This is the block-side face of the props hoist owned by audit/records/seam/creature_card_cmds.json G1, whose census of looser-gating listeners omits this power; carried per binding rule 3, not re-argued. LIVE, and reachable with NO relic: Entrench.cs:23 is the game's only `ValueProp.Unpowered | ValueProp.Move` block gain and it carries a cardPlay, `unmovable` is in IRONCLAD_POOL, and `entrench` is granted by the ported Trash Heap event (sts2_rl/events/trash_heap.py:17). EXECUTED: sim Entrench from 10 block with Unmovable 1 yields 20; C# yields 30. Control: a powered Defend doubles correctly in the sim, proving only the Unpowered arm is missing. The sim's own docstring at powers.py:1086-1088 states the false premise verbatim and is what the old verdict was read off (PROMPT.md bug class 12/24). Found by the relic-tier rule-3 review; `py audit/tools/power_slot_probes.py ungated-modifiers` already listed UnmovablePower.cs:21 as UNGATED and no record had run it. The existing pin test/test_hook_order.py::TestCreatureCardCmdsOrder::test_unpowered_card_block_still_runs_block_modifiers covers the fix. NOTE C#'s predicate also admits monster-MOVE block; that arm stays unreachable here because the owner is always the player. Third-file citations, not hashed here.
